newsitem.title: USA: Final services for Cardinal Bernardin of Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Final services for Cardinal Bernardin of Chicago.

text.p: Church leaders crowded in a cathedral and hundreds of faithful standing outside in the cold heard Cardinal Joseph Bernardin eulogised on Wednesday as a teacher, leader and friend.

"What a presence he had in this church of Chicago. Didn't he teach us? Didn't he show us the way?" long-time aide Msgr. Kenneth Velo said in a homily interrupted once by applause and given a standing ovation at its close.

"He took hard stands -- the consistent ethic of life, nuclear disarmament, racial injustice. He stood on the Capitol steps against partial birth abortions. And in his last days he spoke out loud and clear to the Supreme Court about assisted suicide."
Many of the 1,300 inside Holy Name Cathedral wept as Velo told human and spirtual anecdotes about the Roman Catholic Church's senior U.S. figure, who died last week of cancer at the age of 68.

All nine surving U.S. cardinals and a number from around the world were present at the funeral Mass, along with more than 150 bishops. Many of them knew the South Carolina son of Italian immigrants from his decades-long role as organiser and leader of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops.
Vice President Al Gore and his wife led a delegation of government leaders that included several members of President Bill Clinton's Cabinet.
Bernardin was to buried later in the day in a cemetery near Chicago following a procession winding through neighbourhoods of the 2.3 million-member archdiocese, second largest in the United States.

Velo recounted Bernardin's career from his ordination in 1952 through his service as a bishop in Atlanta and Cincinnati until he arrived in Chicago in 1982 to confront a church community torn by dissent and a financial scandal involving the previous cardinal.
"In this darkened cathedral and darkened archdiocese he brought the light of Christ," Velo said. "He brought life and light that continues to this day..."

More than 90,000 people passed by Bernardin's open casket during an around-the-clock visitation that began on Monday and ended shortly before Wednesday's Mass celebrated by Cardinal Roger Mahoney of Los Angeles.
